'''Decipher era''' is the printed-card period of ''Star Wars'' CCG, from [[Premiere Limited]] in December 1995 through [[Theed Palace]] in December 2001.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016121021/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive]</ref> The publisher was [[Decipher]] of Norfolk, Virginia. The complete constructed pool is [[Premiere - Theed Palace]] (GEMP '''Decipher Cards Only''', <code>open_no_virtual</code>).

== Products and editions ==

The early expansions developed the original trilogy's characters and settings. [[A New Hope Limited]] added creatures, Epic Events and the Death Star mobile location. [[Cloud City Limited]] explored bounty hunting and carbon-freezing. [[Jabba's Palace Limited]] extended those themes into Jabba's court and the rescue of Han Solo.<ref name="decipher-collection">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars CCG: The Expansions], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

The product line also offered ways to begin with fixed cards. The two introductory games supplied decks for both sides. [[Official Tournament Sealed Deck]] combined eighteen fixed cards with booster packs for sealed-deck play. [[First Anthology]] and [[Second Anthology]] bundled earlier packs with preview cards from forthcoming expansions. [[Enhanced Premiere]] paired a new character-and-weapon card with Premiere packs.<ref name="decipher-collection" />

White-border [[Premiere Unlimited]] followed the black-border base set. [[Revised A New Hope]] and [[Revised Hoth]] combined white borders with changes to game text. [[Special Edition]] introduced side-specific starters and included the revised rulebook and glossary with each deck.<ref name="decipher-collection" />

See [[Translations of SWCCG]] for the Japanese editions published by [[Takara]] and the German and Spanish release programs. The released Japanese expansions and introductory games are listed below.

== Sets ==

Decipher sold booster expansions alongside fixed-card products, sealed-deck boxes and anthology collections. The anthologies introduced preview or premium cards while bundling packs and starters from earlier releases.<ref name="decipher-collection">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars CCG: The Expansions], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

Card counts distinguish new cards, alternate images, foil subsets and game aids. A starter row gives the number of cards in a deck. Random reprints packed with Reflections or premium products do not increase their listed set sizes.<ref name="decipher-collecting">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], collecting catalog, pp. 4–45 and 201–202. The primary release notices for the later dates have not yet been located. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

=== Cancelled and planned sets ===

Decipher announced four further expansions after [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]], with the planned dates below.<ref name="decipher-planned">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/whatisit/afterdeathstar.html After Death Star II], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050307015419id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/whatisit/afterdeathstar.html Internet Archive].</ref>
The later [[Reflections Gold]] project also remained unreleased. In January 2002, [[Warren Holland]] announced that Lucasfilm had refused a proposed free PDF of 200 approved cards.<ref name="decipher-gold">Warren Holland, [http://www.decipher.com/starwars/reflectionsgold.html Star Wars Reflections Gold Announcement], Decipher (25 January 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080207033202id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/reflectionsgold.html Internet Archive].</ref>
[[Reflections Gold Remastered]] is an independent remastered edition documented alongside the surviving original playtest material on [[Reflections Gold]].

== Rules ==

Decipher developed the rules through starter-deck booklets, expansion supplements, FAQs, a revised rulebook and glossary, and later rulesheets and glossary updates. [[Rulebooks]] links the original documents and their wiki reading copies.

=== Booklets and expansion supplements ===

The [[Premiere Limited]] starters supplied the [[Premiere starter deck rulebook]], a 40-page booklet titled ''The Rules'' published in 1995.<ref name="premiere-rules-history">Decipher, ''The Rules'' (1995), [[Media:Decipher_Premiere_Starter_Deck_Rulebook_1995.pdf|Premiere starter deck rulebook]], pp. 1–40.</ref> Introductory two-player products also included rulebooks. The booklet in [[The Empire Strikes Back Introductory Two-Player Game]] contained all the Premiere rules and was their most up-to-date version before Special Edition.<ref name="early-rules-history">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/ Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Rules], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980506111511/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/ Internet Archive, 6 May 1998].</ref>

[[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]], [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]], [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] and [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] added rules supplements for their expansions. [[First Anthology]] and [[Official Tournament Sealed Deck]] also had supplements.<ref name="early-rules-history" /><ref name="faq-history-1997">[http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/faq061897.pdf Frequently Asked Questions: Second Partial Preliminary FAQ], Decipher (18 June 1997), p. 1. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980717002749/http://decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/faq061897.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

=== FAQs and Current Rulings ===

Decipher maintained a FAQ alongside the rules documents. Its June 1997 revision appeared in partial releases on 5 and 18 June. The second release identified the Empire Strikes Back two-player booklet and First Anthology supplement as the current rules documents that the FAQ supplemented and clarified.<ref name="faq-history-1997" /> FAQ answers were rulings, distinct from the rulebooks and published changes to card text. After the Glossary replaced the FAQ in November 1998, Decipher continued issuing ''Current Rulings'' updates for gameplay questions requiring clarification.<ref name="faq-history-replaced">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game: FAQs], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19981202133641/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/faqs/index.html Internet Archive, 2 December 1998].</ref>

=== Special Edition revision ===

[[Special Edition]] brought a major revision in November 1998. Each Light Side or Dark Side starter included [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game RULEBOOK 2.0|Rulebook 2.0]] and [[Decipher Glossary 2.0|Glossary 2.0]]. The new rulebook replaced the rules documents published before Special Edition, while the Glossary replaced the FAQ.<ref name="se-rules-history">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Rules], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990428184433/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/productlibrary/rules/index.html Internet Archive, 28 April 1999].</ref>

The online ''Glossary and Current Rules'', Version 2.1, was updated on 1 October 1999. It combined Glossary 2.0, the [[Enhanced Premiere Rulesheet|Enhanced Premiere]] and [[Endor Rulesheet|Endor]] rulesheets, and the September 1999 Current Rulings document in an alphabetical reference.<ref name="online-rules-history">[http://decipher.com/starwars/rules/glossary/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game Online Glossary and Current Rules, Version 2.1], Decipher (updated 1 October 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991012154128/http://decipher.com/starwars/rules/glossary/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

=== Later rulesheets and glossary updates ===

Later products continued adding rulesheets and rule cards, including [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]], [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]], [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]], [[Reflections III]] and [[Theed Palace]].<ref name="later-rules-history">[http://decipher.com/starwars/rules/ Star Wars Customizable Card Game: Rules], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020616214849/http://decipher.com/starwars/rules/ Internet Archive, 16 June 2002].</ref> The ''Supplement to Glossary'' dated 30 May 2001 collected updates, corrections, new rulings and the rule notes from products released after Special Edition.<ref name="supplement-history-2001">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgsupplement053001.pdf Supplement to Glossary], Decipher (30 May 2001), p. 1. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010613012725/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgsupplement053001.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> The [[Decipher Glossary Supplement]] was subsequently updated on 29 January 2002, after the final printed expansion.<ref name="supplement-history-2002">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossarysupplement.pdf Glossary Supplement], Decipher (updated 29 January 2002), p. 1. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041106202626/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossarysupplement.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

== Organized play ==

Decipher ran six World Championships from 1996 through 2001.<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Internet Archive, 17 August 2023]</ref> Each year's constructed pool was printed sets through the newest expansion.

== End of the era ==

Lucasfilm did not renew Decipher's ''Star Wars'' license at the end of 2001.<ref name="wp" /> Stewardship passed to the [[Players Committee]] in 2002. Successor era: [[Virtual Original]].
